plans.note: Only the preamble is exposed in the outline; a Master Services Agreement of this type will carry a limitation of liability article in the body. Search the full text for cap language, exclusion of consequential damages, and whether the cap is mutual and carved out for indemnity, confidentiality, IP and willful misconduct.

Expect a vendor indemnity article in the unexposed body. Confirm Kubient indemnifies AP for third-party IP infringement and its own negligence/misconduct, and that any AP-side indemnity is narrow (limited to AP-supplied content/materials).

No restrictive-covenant section appears in the outline; non-competes are uncommon in an ad-tech MSA. Scan the body for any covenant limiting AP's ability to operate competing businesses or use competing platforms before concluding it is absent.
No exclusivity section surfaced. Check the services/scope and any order form or exhibit for sole-source or 'exclusive provider of programmatic inventory' language that would bind AP.

No pricing section visible. Direction rule: an MFN favouring AP is fine and should not be flagged; only a clause requiring AP to grant Kubient its best terms would be a deviation. Check fees/pricing provisions.
Check the miscellaneous/general provisions in the body for a mutual or one-way non-solicit; if present, test for duration (12 months or less), employee scope, and a general-advertising carve-out.

The preamble references a defined 'Initial Term', so a term and termination article exists in the unexposed body. Locate it and test AP's right to terminate for convenience on notice without penalty, and whether Kubient has a symmetrical mid-term exit.
Tied to the defined 'Initial Term' — review the same term article for auto-renewal, the length of renewal periods, the non-renewal notice window, and any price uplift on renewal.

Expect governing law/venue in the general provisions at the end. Kubient is New York-based, so New York law and New York courts are likely and acceptable; flag only foreign law or mandatory offshore arbitration.

Look in the general provisions for the assignment clause; confirm AP may assign to affiliates and to a successor by merger or asset sale without consent, and that Kubient cannot terminate on an AP change of control.

Direction rule. Find the intellectual property / data article and confirm AP retains ownership of its content, inventory data and any deliverables it pays for; flag any assignment or broad licence of AP data to Kubient beyond what is needed to run the service.
Review the licence/access grant for the platform: scope should extend to AP affiliates and contractors acting on AP's behalf and must not be revocable at Kubient's discretion.

Check for a Kubient right to audit AP's usage or records (often folded into fees/reporting). Test frequency, prior notice, business-hours/off-site limits and who bears cost; audits of Kubient by AP are in our favour and are not flagged.

Direction rule. Service credits or SLA credits running to AP are welcome and should not be flagged; scan the fees and termination provisions for early-termination fees, penalties or liquidated damages payable by AP.

Locate the representations and warranties article; confirm a performance/conformity warranty from Kubient with a meaningful duration and a repair/re-perform or refund remedy, and check whether a broad 'AS IS' disclaimer guts it.

Insurance is often omitted from short ad-tech MSAs. Search the body and any exhibit for commercial general liability, tech E&O and cyber coverage; if none exists, treat as missing since Kubient handles AP inventory and data.
Check the fees section, any order form or insertion order for minimum spend, minimum volume or take-or-pay commitments on AP, and whether an exit or true-up exists.

Review the effects-of-termination provisions for return or deletion of AP data in a usable format and any wind-down/transition assistance; if only deletion is addressed, the transition-assistance element is missing.
